hints.title: Bidirectional Friendship Graph
hints.text: Friendship is symmetric. Build a view or cte containing all direct friend pairs (u, v) and (v, u).

hints.title: Finding Common Friends
hints.text: For each existing edge (u1, u2) where u1 < u2, count common neighbors who are friends with both u1 and u2.

hints.title: Filtering by Threshold
hints.text: Group by u1 and u2 and require the common friend count to be at least 3.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH AllFriends AS (
    SELECT user1_id AS u1, user2_id AS u2 FROM Friendship
    UNION ALL
    SELECT user2_id AS u1, user1_id AS u2 FROM Friendship
)
SELECT
    f.user1_id,
    f.user2_id,
    COUNT(af1.u2) AS common_friend
FROM Friendship f
JOIN AllFriends af1
    ON f.user1_id = af1.u1
JOIN AllFriends af2
    ON f.user2_id = af2.u1
    AND af1.u2 = af2.u2
GROUP BY f.user1_id, f.user2_id
HAVING COUNT(af1.u2) >= 3;
```

complexity.time: O(F * D) where F is friendships and D is max degree
complexity.space: O(F) space for symmetric graph view
variables: F: number of friendship records in Friendship
complexity.notes: Symmetric edge union joined on shared adjacent neighbor.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Looking only at directed friendship misses common friends stored in the reverse direction.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bidirectional union guarantees every mutual neighbor is discovered.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should ensure user1_id < user2_id and common_friend >= 3.

solutions.approach: Bidirectional CTE with mutual neighbor join in MySQL
